title: Liquid Verbs; Reflexive Pronouns
description: The future and first aorist of liquid verbs, the future of εἰμί, and the reflexive pronouns.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html: Liquid verbs have stems ending in λ, μ, ν or ρ. Their future adds ε instead of σ, and the ε contracts with the ending like a verb in -έω: κρινῶ, κρινεῖς, κρινεῖ, κρινοῦμεν, κρινεῖτε, κρινοῦσι(ν). Their first aorist drops the σ and lengthens the stem vowel instead: ἔκρινα, ἀπέστειλα (στελ-), ἔμεινα (μεν-), ἦρα (ἀρ-), ἤγειρα (ἐγερ-). Many liquid verbs have a shorter stem in the future than in the present: βάλλω, βαλῶ; ἀποστέλλω, ἀποστελῶ; ἐγείρω, ἐγερῶ.

blocks.caption: Future of εἰμί
blocks.html: ἔσομαι, ἔσῃ, ἔσται, ἐσόμεθα, ἔσεσθε, ἔσονται: middle forms with the meaning I shall be.

blocks.caption: Reflexive pronouns
blocks.html: The reflexive refers back to the subject: ἐμαυτοῦ (of myself), σεαυτοῦ (of yourself), ἑαυτοῦ, ἑαυτῆς (of himself, of herself). They have no nominative. In the plural ἑαυτῶν serves all three persons: οὐκ ἐγεροῦμεν ἑαυτούς, we shall not raise ourselves. ἀλλήλων, of one another, is reciprocal: ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους, love one another.

blocks.caption: Common confusion
blocks.html: μένει (he remains) and μενεῖ (he will remain) differ only in the accent; κρίνει and κρινεῖ likewise. On the top rung the accent decides.
